artists.biography: Todd Harry Rundgren (born June 22, 1948) is an American multi-instrumentalist, songwriter and record producer. Hailed in the early stage of his career as a new pop star, supported by the certified gold solo double LP Something/Anything? in 1972, his career has produced a diverse range of recordings as solo artist, and during the seventies and eighties with the band Utopia. He has also been prolific as a producer and engineer on the recorded work of other musicians.

A close listen to the album reveals the eccentricities and restless spirit that surges to the forefront on its follow-up, A Wizard, A True Star. Anyone expecting the third record of Something/Anything?, filled with variations on "I Saw the Light" and "Hello It\'s Me," will be shocked by A Wizard. perplexity.description:
Released in March 1973 on Bearsville Records, A Wizard, a True Star is Todd Rundgren’s fourth studio album and a radical departure from the straightforward pop-rock of his previous breakthrough, Something/Anything?. Recorded at his newly built Secret Sound studio in New York, the album is a kaleidoscopic fusion of electronic experimentation, rock, psychedelia, and pop, featuring layered synthesizers, abrupt stylistic shifts, and a stream-of-consciousness approach. The record’s 55-minute runtime unfolds as a continuous suite, blending lush harmonies, avant-garde textures, and moments of pure whimsy, reflecting Rundgren’s desire to capture the chaos of his creative mind without commercial compromise.

In the context of Rundgren’s discography, A Wizard, a True Star stands as a bold, idiosyncratic statement following his mainstream success. Eschewing singles and conventional structure, the album marked a turning point in his career, alienating some fans but earning admiration from fellow musicians and critics for its ambition and innovation. Upon release, it received mixed reviews and peaked at #86 on the Billboard 200, yet it has since been recognized as a pioneering work in electronic and psychedelic rock, influencing artists across genres and cementing its status as a cult classic.
